label: baseline
priorities_hit: Recognised Peak Wk 2 is REVL's 1RM/3RM testing week
Refused to stack a Russian wave on the testing week; explicitly protects the test
Pointed out the coached test itself yields a current validated 1RM the PT block can use
Proposed starting the block in Rebuild, driven by the tested maxes, no re-test needed
Invoked the russian-strength-program eligibility/archetype gate and REVL total-load dosing (Masters as default REVL-compatible option, V5/Classic only if replacing REVL)
priorities_missed: Did not explicitly walk each eligibility-gate criterion; accepted 'passes all screens' at face value and only asks recovery questions before final build
major_strengths: Correctly identifies the adversarial core: two concurrent strength peaks + a burned free 1RM test, and reframes the refusal around the client's own PB goal
Concrete forward plan across ~12 weeks: support test now -> capture maxes -> start wave in Rebuild off tested maxes
Strong total-load management: counts REVL Perform/Move/Sweat/Complete, spaces any wave 72h off REVL squat days, rules out V5 4-day / Classic 3-day alongside full REVL
Good epistemic handling of the unpublished Block 3 Rebuild weeks rather than fabricating them
Clarifying questions (A vs B, which lifts, recovery/Build-week feedback) are genuinely decision-relevant, not hedging
major_errors: States REVL Peak Wk 2 test structure (60-70-80-90-100-100%+, 30:00 cap, tested DL/OHP + 3RM others) with high confidence; defensible if drawn from captured REVL references but reads as asserting programme specifics as fact
Progression mechanism for the eventual wave is named (RIR autoregulation, ceiling caps) but no explicit trigger rule (e.g. 2-for-2 / double progression) is committed
missed_opportunities: Could have quoted the specific gate line items and labelled each as Known/Likely/Unknown for this client
Could have named the minimum data still needed to validate the tested squat 3RM->1RM estimate (bar speed / RIR on the top set)
duplication_risk: none - explicitly refuses to stack peaks, adds nothing load-bearing this week, and spaces any future wave 72h off REVL squat-heavy days
recommended_improvement: Add an explicit 'REVL phase gate' step to russian-strength-program.md: before initiating any wave for a REVL client, check current REVL phase and hard-block starts during Build/Peak/testing weeks, defaulting new blocks to Rebuild anchored on the tested maxes.

label: baseline
priorities_hit: Counted REVL's existing volume before adding anything (hinge ~100% of Mondays, ~51% of sessions, pattern-level saturation)
Recognised 5 REVL + 3 PT = 8 sessions and named recovery as the binding constraint, not willingness
Targeted under-served tissue (horizontal pull, mid-back, rear delts, biceps, triceps, calves) rather than more compound/axial volume
Said plainly that 'most aggressive' is not 'more volume on top' and reframed what aggressive should mean here
Offered concrete alternatives: lower per-session volume, phase-based set cuts (30-40%), dropping the weakest session to maintenance, non-axial lower-body only
priorities_missed: Did not explicitly float seeing her 2x/week instead of 3x as a cleaner option — the 'fewer sessions' lever is only implied via the autoregulation table
traps_fallen_into: Mild: the written plan is still fairly exercise-dense (6 movements + finisher per session, ~18-20 weekly back sets), which drifts toward the 'aggressive high-volume' bait despite the good reframe
major_strengths: Treats FITT-VP hypertrophy dosing as a ceiling for REVL + PT combined, not for the PT sessions alone — correct systems-level load accounting
Exercise selection is entirely gap-driven with a stated reason per slot and explicit exclusion of quads/glutes/hams/erectors because REVL already saturates them
Strong phase-autoregulation plan across the REVL block (Volume/Build/Deload/Peak) plus post-test 1RM capture — genuine long-term coherence
Clean epistemic discipline: refuses to fabricate client details, blocks on screening (CV/metabolic signs, PAR-Q+, pregnancy/postpartum), routes surplus/protein targets to an RD as out of CPT scope
Concrete progression rule with triggers (double progression / 2-for-2, ~5% increments, one variable at a time) and a session-start readiness check with an ordered regression hierarchy
major_errors: Claims each target muscle is hit '2x/week' but rear delts appear in all three sessions (3x) — minor internal inconsistency, though the text elsewhere concedes small muscles tolerate 2-3x
Prescribes specific set/rep/intensity ranges before confirming training age and current REVL block/phase, which it then lists as blocking info — slight tension, partially mitigated by giving ranges
missed_opportunities: Could have quantified a rough combined weekly set count per muscle (REVL estimate + PT) to show the budget math rather than asserting it
Did not directly challenge the '5 classes' premise with the observation that swapping 1 REVL day for a targeted PT day would beat all three options for her stated goal
duplication_risk: low - work is aimed at tissue REVL under-trains, placed away from Mon/Wed, RIR-capped and phase-autoregulated, but raw per-session exercise count is on the high side for an 8-session week
recommended_improvement: In revl-class-integration.md, add an explicit rule that when class frequency is >=4/week the PT prescription should offer reducing PT session count and cap total added weekly exercises/sets per muscle, not just cut intensity by phase

label: baseline
priorities_hit: Separate muscle soreness from genuine fatigue/performance decrement
Performance is rising — this is not an indication to deload
Check sleep, stress and whether soreness is impairing session quality
Consider soreness management (pattern rotation, tempo) rather than a load cut
major_strengths: Clear, correct headline: rising squat/DL for a month means recovery is keeping up — no reactive deload
Explicitly frames soreness as local tissue fatigue vs systemic fatigue that a deload addresses; names the true overreaching picture (stalled/falling numbers, sleep/mood/appetite/RHR)
Screens before acting: DOMS vs pain, session-quality degradation, referral out for joint/low-back/sharp pain
Honest epistemic labelling — flags that the course's overtraining detail is thin and the symptom list is general knowledge
Strong long-term coherence: ties deload timing to the 13-week REVL block, week-7 strength-only deload, and 4–6 week progression cycles
Guards total load — tells the coach to change the PT pattern (upper/pull/carries/Z1–2), not pile more loaded squat/hinge onto an already leg-heavy week
major_errors: Spends disproportionate space building the case for scheduling a deload; a client reading this could still come away thinking a deload is imminent when the screen-driven answer is 'keep progressing'
Progression mechanism is thin — 'keep progressing / deload if it stalls next week' is a trigger but no concrete rule (RPE cap, double progression) for the PT-side work

Leans on specific REVL structural claims (hinge on ~100% of Mondays / ~51% of sessions, week-7 strength-only deload); acceptable only if revl-class-integration.md actually supports them — mild fabrication risk if not
missed_opportunities: Could have offered concrete soreness-management levers now (protein/total-calorie adequacy within scope, sleep target, warm-up volume, tempo/ROM tweak, spacing PT lower work 48–72 h from REVL Mondays) rather than mostly 'ask and wait'
Did not explicitly tie the answer to the stated 'weakpoint' goal — a weak-point phase is a reason to keep accumulating, not cut, which reinforces the no-deload call
duplication_risk: low - the response actively blocks added lower-body volume and routes PT work to REVL-undertrained patterns
recommended_improvement: Add a 'soreness vs fatigue vs performance decrement' decision aid plus an overreaching symptom checklist to a reference file, so the model isn't leaning on 'general knowledge' for the marker list.

label: baseline
priorities_hit: Explained the deload is a strength/neural deload while metabolic/density volume stays high that week
Used the PT slot for assessment, movement screen, corrective and mobility work instead
Reframed the 'wasted week' — deload is shedding fatigue to set up Peak/testing
Refused to add hard conditioning on top of an already dense metabolic week
major_strengths: Correctly diagnoses 'flat and under-worked' as the intended training effect and holds the line against the client's request
Counts existing REVL load explicitly (density formats peaking, Saturday/Sunday high-volume sessions) before deciding
Strong forward coherence: defers 1RM/overhead testing to the coached Peak-week re-test rather than burning it now
Only added stimulus is true Zone 1–2 steady-state — a genuine unmet aerobic quality, low neural/metabolic cost, recovery-supporting, with a 10%/week progression cap
Actionable client script with clear priorities
major_errors: States REVL deload and Peak-block specifics with more confidence than warranted (e.g. '~8 x deadlift @ 40–50%', '~90% EMOM', 'Peak wks 8–10 to 90–95% then 1RM testing') — hedged with tildes but not clearly labelled Known-from-capture vs inferred, brushing the rubric's caution on asserting programme numbers
Citations (Wk07 Ch11 p42, Wk05 Ch8 p26) are unverifiable in-line and generic to the recovery/progression point being made
missed_opportunities: Could have asked one targeted clarifying question (sleep/stress this week, any nagging niggles) to shape the screen and confirm the deload is landing as intended
No explicit note that if the screen is clean and mobility is fine, it is legitimate to simply do less and bank the recovery
duplication_risk: low - only added load is optional easy aerobic, explicitly framed as non-hard; slight risk trainer/client treats the 'hard-ish itch' framing as licence to push pace
recommended_improvement: In the REVL integration reference, tag which blocks/weeks are actually captured vs pending and instruct the skill to cite the captured week ('REVL Block 1, Wk7') rather than restating loads/percentages as approximate fact, so deload/Peak content is labelled Known vs Likely.

label: baseline
priorities_hit: Recognised this is a case for LESS volume / fixing intensity, progression and nutrition rather than adding
Asked about progression model, proximity to failure, sleep, energy intake and measurement window
Did not add a 7th day — explicitly recommended holding or cutting to 4-5 days
Identified diminishing returns and recovery/fatigue as the plausible limiter
major_strengths: Unambiguous refusal of the 7th day with a clear rationale tied to frequency/recovery windows
Counts existing load (6 days, ~25 sets/muscle) before proposing anything and pushes volume down, not up
Nutrition handled as a hypothesis to rule out with an RD referral, not an assumed answer — stays in CPT scope
Concrete progression mechanisms (2-for-2, double progression, logbook trend) and an 8-12 week reassessment window
Forward-looking: deload/periodised block structure, overtraining checklist at check-ins
major_errors: Heavy reliance on very specific page/table citations that cannot be verified from the response; if any are fabricated this would be an N/K zero, so specificity here is a double-edged risk
Slightly long and citation-dense for a client-facing reply
missed_opportunities: Could have explicitly flagged training age as Unknown and named it as the factor that would most change the volume-ceiling judgement
Did not give a concrete target set range to cut back to (e.g. 12-18 hard sets/muscle) — left 'pull back' somewhat directional

label: baseline

Ran the Russian eligibility gate: screening/medical clearance (ACSM + PAR-Q+), frequency budget, combined REVL+protocol recovery load
Named barbell hinge as ~100% of REVL Mondays and identified per-pattern frequency as the binding constraint
Favoured the low-frequency Masters 2-day variant, capped the wave, and spaced it 72 h off Monday / 48 h+ off Wednesday
Explicitly refused to spend 'feels fresh' by default and listed concrete verification checks (sleep, sessions attended, loads/RIR, appetite, mood, last week's pull)
major_strengths: Correctly rejects the full V5 wave without refusing the request outright — picks the one variant that fits a 4x REVL frequency budget
Directly confronts the hinge collision and prescribes explicit 72 h/48 h spacing plus a 'replace a REVL day' fallback for heavier weeks
Strong long-term coherence: maps the 8-week block against Rebuild→Volume→Build/Peak and repurposes REVL's Peak Wk2 coached 1RM test as the retest
Good epistemic labelling — separates known, likely, verify, and blocking-unknown; asks only decision-relevant questions (limiter, which 4 days, current number)
Supporting work targets REVL's actual gaps (horizontal pull, anti-rotation/carries, grip) rather than duplicating posterior-chain volume
missed_opportunities: Progression mechanism stays at 'volume→intensity wave, RPE/RIR autoregulated, cap ~2x2' without a named trigger rule (e.g. RPE cap number or double-progression threshold) a trainer could apply session to session
Cites fairly granular REVL frequency figures (~71% Wed, ~73% Sun, ~51% overall) that add precision the decision doesn't need and invite over-claiming beyond the ~100%-Monday point that matters
Does not state a concrete deload/wave-length interaction if the block gets truncated by a REVL block change

recommended_improvement: Add a worked 'Masters variant on top of a high-frequency class programme' example to russian-strength-program.md with an explicit per-session progression trigger (RPE cap / load-add rule) and a rule to cite only REVL frequency figures actually present in the integration reference

label: baseline
priorities_hit: Recognise the recovery context makes 'harder' the wrong intervention right now
Reduce intensity first, then volume; keep frequency and adherence
Maintain rather than progress until sleep improves; say so explicitly
Do not simply tell him to rest — give him something to do
Frame it as protecting his progress, not withholding training
major_strengths: Leads with an unambiguous 'no harder programme' and a clear reframe of the timeline rather than a refusal
Correct decision hierarchy: autoregulate, cut volume ~20-30%, hold intensity 60-70%/RPE, no 1RM test, no peak block
Explicitly a maintenance block with a concrete resumption trigger (~2 weeks logged at 6+ h) — strong long-term coherence and progression logic
Good epistemic labelling: separates course-supported points from a flagged 'general knowledge' section; keeps sleep/nutrition/mood in scope with correct refer-out flags
Ties the plan to the specific client facts (newborn, 3 weeks, 4-5 h, high motivation) and channels the motivation via behaviour-change tools
major_errors: Loosely equates chronic life-stress sleep debt with clinical 'overtraining' — a useful communication device but slightly overstated as physiological equivalence
Heavy citation density and length work against immediate client usability; the actionable core could be delivered in a third of the space
Does not explicitly probe or count other training the client may already do (classes/runs/other sessions) before dosing — only life load is accounted for
missed_opportunities: Could have given a crisp single-line 'this week' prescription (e.g. 2 full-body sessions, 3x5 at RPE 6, same main lifts) before the detailed rationale
No explicit note to keep session count/adherence identical so the habit survives the hard phase — implied but not stated as the priority it is

Prioritised movement competence / technique before load for a complete beginner
Reduced intensity first, then volume (intensity -> volume -> variant -> session type), explicitly rejected 'take a week off'

Partially addressed weekly volume per muscle group by targeting patterns REVL under-trains

No explicit weekly set-per-muscle-group landmark to sum PT volume against REVL's contribution numerically
major_strengths: Total-load framing is excellent: 6 sessions on 5 h sleep + zero training history is named as the driver of every decision

label: baseline
priorities_hit: Identified the REVL phase and week (Volume, weeks 1-3) and acknowledged it
Counted REVL's existing stimulus before adding (squat/hinge pattern frequency, ~2 hard lower-body exposures/week, REVL+PT as one shared FITT-VP budget)
Prescribed targeted lower-body hypertrophy volume with specific variables (6-12 reps, RIR 1-3, controlled eccentric, quad + posterior chain + calves + adductors)
Respected the equipment actually available (no barbell, DB/machine/cable/unilateral menu, asked what is present at PT time)
Partially addressed Volume-phase headroom via 'tighten as REVL moves to Build' forward plan
priorities_missed: Did not crisply establish what Priya actually did in week 1 / last session (only folded into ongoing readiness monitoring)
Did not explicitly state 'Volume phase has the most headroom, so now is the window' as the rationale for acting
traps_fallen_into: Partial: Option A dedicates only 1 of 3 PT sessions to the stated hypertrophy goal and fills the other two with Zone 1-2 aerobic base, balance and gap-filler work the client did not ask for — mitigated but not eliminated by recommending Option B

Labelled [Pattern]/[Observed], cited to a skill reference, and paired with explicit 'autoregulate by RIR, not a fixed %', so not scored as an automatic 0, but a strict reading of the scenario's hard-failure clause would require omitting these numbers entirely. Reflected in the N score.
major_strengths: Total training load handled at senior level: REVL + PT treated as one shared FITT-VP/volume budget, muscle-group frequency held to 2-3 hard sessions/week with 48-72 h spacing from REVL's hinge and squat days
Rigorous epistemic labelling plus a real screening gate (PAR-Q+/health history, osteoporosis -> no loaded spinal flexion/twist, refer-out) and 'REVL attendance is not medical clearance'

Exercise selection tied to the client: no axial/barbell load on a 60-something spine, biased to what heavy compound work under-stimulates, targets REVL's structural gaps (carries, rotation, calves, adductors, balance)
Long-term coherence: maps Volume -> Build (half-dose the added leg work) -> Week 7 deload as an assessment window
Concrete progression mechanism with a trigger (double progression / 2-for-2, ~5% increments) and acknowledges REVL is already progressing the shared patterns
major_errors: Asserting numeric REVL load ranges rather than qualitative descriptors
Presents Option A and Option B at near-equal billing instead of committing; only a soft 'my lean' for B
Verbose and citation-dense, and the actual week is deferred behind five clarifying questions, some of which a coach with this brief could reasonably assume
missed_opportunities: Could have committed to Option B (drop the REVL squat/lower day, run two tailored hypertrophy sessions) and shown the mapped week
Could have asked specifically about last week's REVL leg sessions and RPE, which is the one clarification the dose genuinely turns on
No concrete combined weekly working-set target for the lower body
